title: Conrad Biermann to Paul von Klingenberg at The Hague, 1675: the Klingenberg cipher of the Biermann copybook (Rigsarkivet, TKUA; catalogue 465), key rebuilt from the ciphertext, read in part

steps.what: The repository's lead, Chiffer sheet 94/95, tested on the Klingenberg letters: held-out letters 0 of 305 and 0 of 144. Not the key.
Letter signs from a probable word, requisition, which also stands in the clear text of the 6 February letter, and from repeats.
Syllable table 437-525 as alphabetical rows, from alliierten and other repeated forms, fitted on four March letters; 16 March held out: 36 of 157 tokens strict with the table alone.
Greedy fit of the 30 most frequent numbers below 430 to German function words with a quadgram model: degenerate (er, in, ge everywhere).

Word-code values from two or more independent contexts in training letters: map v1 (29 May held out, 284 of 437), v2 (17 April held out, 165 of 239), v3 with 78 values (4 May held out: 551 of 729 = 75.6%). A parser fault of the first scripts (lines beginning with the sign # skipped) was found and fixed.

Word-map values shuffled over the same codes, 5,000 times, each letter re-scored against its gloss: 0 of 5,000 reach the real count on any letter. The gloss was written after decoding by the same judge, so this control is weaker than it looks.

Seven untouched copybook letters (8 May to 24 June), each transcribed, frozen and decoded once with v3 unchanged: 2,006 of 2,524 tokens (79.5%). Then map v4 (106 values). Three drafts from the next archive unit, decoded once with v4 unchanged: 1,091 of 1,456 (74.9%).

Check by Daniel Bourdeau on issue 424: a decoder written from the key reproduces all 452 sign and syllable tokens of the 4 May letter; 331 of 333 tokens agree with images 166-168; two numerals corrected (447 for 441, probably 501 for 511); 0 of 5,000 for shuffled keys with a German model on the signs and the table; the word-code layer only weakly separated by a character model; 54 open-code tokens, not 42.

For this folder: both numerals checked on the images (447 certain, 501 probable); every figure of the issue recomputed (counts.txt); rule-built readings with every hole in place; full English for the 4 May letter and the three drafts only.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3648 tokens, 201 types, de-modern order 4: reading -2.093 per letter; random keys -4.316 (z 9.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.821 (mean -2.834, z 89.6); annealer on the real text -2.53. Verdict: pass.

Independent verification before the write-up: scripts/count.py re-run in a copy (all lines of counts.txt reproduce); own decoder from key.tsv reproduces the 4 May decryption token for token; frozen-transcription hashes and the three Sectigo tokens checked; Rigsarkivet images fetched and 62 groups of 1 June and 63 of the 28 June draft compared (all agree), 331 of 333 for 4 May by the first verifier; sheet 94/95 compared with the map (117, 140, 200, 224 differ).

PR #490: 22 further passages of the drafts units (260195, 260196) transcribed once each by the first reader (the model that built the key, not blind) from the Rigsarkivet images, decoded once under map v4 (md5 e9698159, table M3 38c7c1e5, unchanged), judged by word units after decoding. First transcriptions and decodes are lines of nine RFC 3161 manifests (Sectigo, 12 Nov 2026 13:21 to 16:26 GMT).

First-reader strict share of the 22 passages: 2,561 of 3,386 word units (75.63%); 6,103 of 8,587 tokens (71.07%, the rule of the count of record); tokens in words with no word code 2,032 of 8,587 (23.66%). No passage reaches 95%. Not added to the count of record (3,648 of 4,709, 77.47%): single not-blind judge, intended words written after decoding.

Blind second transcriptions of all 22 passages by separate model sessions (b158, b161, b166, b172, b176), each decoded once under v4 and judged by word units, '?' units as holes: 16 passages 1,976 of 2,567 (76.98%), last six 579 of 693 (83.55%), all 22 2,555 of 3,260 (78.37%). The readers knew the key; breaches logged (the H/# chart with H = g and # = c seen by b161 and b176; the sign map seen by b172 after freezing 136R; the first reader's file names seen by b166). At six sites the first reader's # is a single-barred H; on 247R a margin cipher insert was missed by both readers; 235L has a margin block in a different cipher outside this key.

Contributor: German 4-gram score of each filed decode against 5,000 shuffles of the word map, two seeds, 0/5,000 for all 22 (script not in the folder; three passages have no output file). One parked passage (134R-136L body) 1/5,000 at one seed, not filed.

Corrected H/# pass on the three July drafts (run b116): hash-like signs re-classified by form against a chart of 12 H and 12 # from the copybook hand, frozen 12 Nov 05:43:43 UTC (md5 acd67760), mapped to 70 positions, decoded once with v4: 1,181 of 1,456 tokens (81.11%). The classifier had read the integration note quoting the 81.5% what-if; no ledger or gloss was written. Not the count of record (74.93%).

Prior art: the printed Privy Council protocol of 1675 (Aarsberetninger fra det Kongelige Geheimearchiv VI, pp. 117-126) and Historisk Tidsskrift 5. R. IV pp. 446-450 checked on archive.org (text of aarsberetninger02wegegoog and historisktidsskriftdk5s4): every quotation of the contributor's evidence file found under the stated printed page. They print the policy of 1675 (fleet subsidies, declaration against Sweden, Lüneburg troops, Bremen, the state before Brömsebro), not a letter to Klingenberg and no cipher. The content of 13 of the 22 drafts is already in print in summary (RISK); for nine nothing found. The matching of drafts to protocol entries is the contributor's, by hand.

Integration check of PR #490 (round 5): ledgers re-parsed (2,561/3,386 and 6,103/8,587 reproduce, per passage); an own decoder from key.tsv, the table and v4 reproduces the decode column of all 22 ledgers (3,386 units, 0 differences); count.py reproduces counts.txt; nine tokens' imprints equal their manifests; 46 of 56 frozen md5 values match files (the other ten are parked passages); images fetched: 136R 79 groups and 214R-216R 124 groups all agree (digits). Own control (de-modern order 4, v4 word values shuffled, 1,000 shuffles): 0 of 1,000 for 13 passages, 1 to 29 of 1,000 for nine.

German reading and English translation of each of the 22 further passages (PR #496), built by rule from the frozen transcription, the single decode with map v4 and the ledger: holes stay in place; an E unit is printed decode[?word] only where the ledger word passes one fixed similarity test (210 of 733 E units); the English by an AI model, not checked by a German reader. No key value added, no figure changed: every passage stays read in part (best 214R-216R at 91.18% of word units).

Integration check of PR #496 (round 6), by own scripts on all 22 passages: stripping our punctuation reproduces each reading line for line; the E-unit table of each reading has as many rows as the ledger has E units and as many printed emendations as the reading has [?word]; the English has every hole in the same order (the six [0] of 287R excepted, as the contributor says); the reading equals the ledger decode on 3,384 of 3,386 units (two blots in one unit shown as one). Five passages read against their English.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.093; polyphony 0.0; 1061 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.53

outcome.method_basis: No key sheet and no decipherment: signs from a probable word and repeats, the syllable table from its alphabetical structure, word-code values from repeated contexts in the letters themselves, each map frozen before the letter it was tested on.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.txt (scripts/count.py): over the eleven letters that were each decoded once with a map frozen beforehand, 3,648 of 4,709 cipher tokens decode exactly to the judge's intended word (4 May 551 of 729; seven copybook letters 2,006 of 2,524; three drafts 1,091 of 1,456). Codes with no value in the map are never counted. The judge's glosses were written after decoding and have not been checked by a second reader.

gaps.item: Word codes with no value in the map of record (54 tokens of the 4 May letter under v3, 25 under v4)
gaps.detail: Mostly names and nouns seen once to five times: 143, 418, 71, 353, 112, 180, 352, 329, 416, 385. More letters, or Klingenberg's own deciphered letterbook, would fix them.

gaps.item: The sign for c against the sign for g in the three drafts
gaps.detail: The reader wrote every hash-like sign as # (c). 96 failed tokens sit in words that differ from the intended word only by c for g. A corrected H/# pass (run b116) gives 1,181 of 1,456 (81.11%), but the classifier had read the 81.5% what-if and wrote no ledger or gloss, so the count of record stays 74.93%; a blind re-reading with a ledger is still owed.

gaps.item: Sixteen further letters (6 February to 21 June) used to build the key
gaps.detail: Transcription and decryption only, with open word codes throughout; no reading and no count of record, since the key was built on them and they cannot be held out. 20 March is its first page only.

gaps.item: Clear text between the cipher passages
gaps.detail: Read approximately; one long clear passage of the 4 May letter only in part.

gaps.item: Prior decipherment in Klingenberg's own papers
gaps.detail: Rigsarkivet guide nos. 278 and 327 not checked; priority is not established.

gaps.item: The 22 further passages (PR #490): 335 of 733 E units hold a code with no value in v4
gaps.detail: 329 occurrences of 111 distinct codes (most often 211, 110, 250, 5, 139, 143, 354; '0' is the O-as-0 slip of 287R-289L). More letters or Klingenberg's deciphered letterbook would fix them.

gaps.item: Ten passages parked by the first reader (59R-60L, 70R, 254R, 263L, 274R, 72L-72R P.S., 112R-113, 134R-136L body, 151R P.S., 152L; 253R-254L not transcribed)
gaps.detail: 112R-113 and 253R-254L are illegible (bleed-through, overwriting). For the others the transcriptions were not sent, only md5 values and logged figures (322 of 455 word units, 70.77%).

texts.label: Biermann to Klingenberg, 4 May 1675
texts.note: read_share is the count of record of counts.txt: 551 of 729 cipher tokens read under map v3 frozen before the letter was first decoded (the one rule of this folder). The contributor's own count by words on the reading file (README word rule) is not used. The glosses were written after decoding by the same model that built the key; see NOTES.
texts.summary: The King has read with surprise that the allies hold him bound to break with Sweden while giving no subsidies for his fleet. The treaty point on the fleet is conditional, but Sweden must be hurt at sea, which cannot be done without a fleet, and Sweden will equip hers; war without a fleet would leave Sweden a free hand. The King has more men on foot than the treaties stipulate and agrees to a muster in his own lands. He has told the resident 'Brendt' how unwillingly he sees the Elector left without earnest support, and takes it as an example; if the allies' principals go on so, he and the Elector can part from the affair with advantage and reputation. Klingenberg is referred to the last letter about co-signing the declaration of war on Sweden. Context: the Scanian War; the Elector of Brandenburg was at The Hague in May 1675.

The Swedish ambassador extraordinary has handed in a new paper, which is to rest until the secretary sent to Sweden returns.

texts.summary: The King has read the reports on the allies' conclusion at The Hague, which Klingenberg and Høeg accepted; though it is not in accordance with his instructions and in many points contrary, he will not disavow them, and he awaits the particulars. They are to press for prompt payment of the remaining and fleet subsidies and the arrears of Anritzgelder, for ships manned for landings and put at the King's disposal, and to divert the allies' plan to send the Lüneburg troops to Flanders: they are needed on the Elbe, and without them the King will hardly proceed to the rupture. [413] [385] salt ships from Lisbon are said to be on the way, whose capture could open the war.

The King agrees that the three thousand boatmen be taken on with his commissaries' billets and pay, as far as possible from his own subjects who are still free [?] (ledig). Høeg's mission to the Elector is not yet decided but will probably go ahead; 6,000 Swedish men are said to stand ready to cross to Germany.

texts.summary: Nothing is added on the Lüneburg troops beyond the dispatch of 25 May. The Swedish ambassador Count Niels Brahe has formally presented his king's marriage suit, and after long delay the King has declared through [193] that it is not contrary to him, with the express rider that the marriage shall not prejudice his treaties with the allies or their execution; Klingenberg is to remove any umbrage the States and the allies take. The King goes to Holstein next week to inspect his troops at Rendsburg and will propose a meeting to the Duke of Gottorp. Context (general knowledge, not from a source here): probably Charles XI of Sweden's suit for the Danish princess Ulrika Eleonora, 1675.

Klingenberg is to guard the King's interest at The Hague; the King would rather be given the further subsidy to strengthen his own troops.
